title: Tenant telemetry drift and dashboard resilience improvements
creator: Amina Patel
description: Multiple customer escalations reported intermittent missing metric series and blank dashboard tiles across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments. Customers observed trace gaps for high-throughput tenants immediately after autocompaction windows and during rebalancer events. Investigation uncovered a race between the telemetry compaction TTL job and the shard rebalancer that could leave recent series metadata unindexed for a short window, causing consumer offsets to skip and frontend dashboards to show empty tiles. This ticket captures the mitigation, bugfix, rollout, and follow-up actions to prevent recurrence and improve tenant-visible resiliency.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No regressions in time-series indexing under standard e2e load tests (synthetic tenants) for 72h; 2) Backfilled missing series for all impacted tenants and verified in dashboards and trace explorer; 3) Canary rollout completed for Hosted, Dedicated and Private with automatic rollback guardrails; 4) Playbook documented and alerted so oncall can detect and remediate faster than current MTTR.
steps_taken: 2026-01-14: Acknowledge customer escalations from 3 enterprise tenants; opened incident bridge and collected logs and customer dashboards.
2026-01-15: Correlated missing metrics with compaction and rebalancer events using ingestion logs and broker offsets; reproduced locally with synthetic tenant generator at ~5k series/min.
2026-01-18: Implemented a short-term mitigation: bump consumer commit behavior to ensure offsets are only advanced after index ack; deployed as hotfix to Hosted to stop new occurrences.

2026-01-20: Implemented root-cause fix in ingestion coordinator: delay TTL compaction of series metadata until shard rebalancer quiescent or until index-writing checkpoint confirmed; added explicit fencing token when rebalancer performs shard move.
2026-01-22: Added defensive dashboard-side fallback to render cached tile content and a soft-warning banner rather than blank tiles if series metadata is missing temporarily.

2026-01-24: Built a backfill tool that replays recent ingestion batches against the index with dedupe by write-id to reconstruct missing series and traces; ran backfill for impacted tenants in Dedicated and Private environments with customer approval.

2026-01-26: Added automated test harness for compaction+rebalancer race and baseline performance test to CI; increased trace sampling for short window to help reconcile spans missed during rebalancer events.
2026-01-30: Canary rollout to Hosted with 10% traffic, monitoring SLOs and alerts; after 48h, promoted to 100% Hosted. Drafted customer-facing remediation summary and shared in support tickets.
2026-02-01: Prepared Private/Dedicated packaging and config flags for customers running air-gapped on-prem; validated upgrade path and rollback.
2026-02-02: Submitted PRs for review and opened this ticket for validation and final signoff.
Notes: All code changes include feature flags to enable/disable the new compaction behavior per-cluster and per-tenant to minimize risk during rollout.
impact_analysis: Root cause is a timing window where the compaction TTL job can drop series metadata before the new in-flight writes are fully checkpointed when a shard moves. Impact varied: Hosted customers saw transient blank tiles; Dedicated customers with high write throughput experienced missing metric series lasting up to several minutes; Private/on-prem customers reported the longest windows if they had older broker versions. No data loss at raw event level was detected; the issue was indexing visibility and consumer offset progression leading to temporary gaps in dashboards and trace stitching.

Investigate whether similar race exists in other index lifecycles (e.g., label-index compaction) and extend tests
Add an opt-in stronger consistency mode for tenants that require no indexing visibility windows (configurable at tenant level)
Rollout dashboard client resilience pattern to other critical tiles (A/B experiment in console-2026.02)
